title: SUPERSEDED: Claude Code rejects dotted MCP tool names -- disproven
summary: An agent-proposed theory that dotted tool names (e.g. estimator.get_project_knowledge) caused Claude Code MCP registration failures was explicitly corrected by the operator and disproven by direct protocol testing: the MCP spec allows '.' in tool names, and the working baseline server (bid-composer-app-mcp) already used dotted names successfully. The real root cause was the unsupported cwd field (see MCP-CWD-UNSUPPORTED-001). Do not rename dotted tool names.
retrievalQuestions: Does the MCP protocol allow dots in tool names, and did Claude Code ever reject dotted tool names?
Should dotted MCP tool names like estimator.get_project_knowledge be renamed to fix registration failures?
What proof disproved the dotted-tool-names root-cause theory for MCP server failures?

futureAgentInstructions.whenThisAppears: A future agent observes a Claude Code MCP server with dotted tool names failing and considers renaming the tools as a fix
startAt: MCP-CWD-UNSUPPORTED-001 seed packet -- the actual root cause
runPreflight: a raw initialize -> notifications/initialized -> tools/list protocol probe against the failing server
doNot: Rename or alias dotted MCP tool names to fix a registration or tool-call failure
Treat a naming-convention correlation as proof of root cause without testing the raw protocol sequence
proveBeforeClaiming: A working, already-deployed server (bid-composer-app-mcp) uses dotted tool names successfully
The MCP specification explicitly permits '.' characters in tool names
